propositions: The check_raw_git_writes gate correctly detects attribute-form git wrapper calls via the ast.Attribute branch in _wrapper_name, but this detection is untested and undocumented, creating a false impression of a blind spot.

The gate has carried the ast.Attribute branch since its first commit (6739ea54fa) alongside ast.Name, confirmed by git log -S; synthetic probes verify core._git(), mod.run_git(), nested receivers, and self._git() all fire as expected.

All 8 existing R2 tests use only bare-name ast.Name form, leaving attribute-form detection entirely unpinned and vulnerable to future refactoring that could remove the branch while tests remain green.

The _ref_lock_push.py file contains no hits not because wrapper calls escape detection but because its only wrapper call (push_lease_cas) passes 'push', which is not in MUTATION_VERBS, so the gate correctly does not fire.

Attribute-form calls and bare-name calls are both silenced identically by the # raw-git-ok marker, and the gate docstring must document that wrapper detection matches on the callable attribute itself regardless of receiver shape.

Four new tests must pin attribute-form detection with various receiver shapes (self, nested, imported-module), fail-closed opaque forwarding, marker sanctioning, and the push-verb negative case to ensure future maintainability.
